name: HYDRA-UMC-LOCAL-TECHNICIAN
build: Six-phase plan (see the README's own Roadmap section): a local, policy-gated AI technician for the ecosystem itself - observes, explains, diagnoses and proposes maintenance, never acts by generating text. The LLM proposes; a deterministic orchestrator validates against real contracts and a real risk-level policy before anything executes, and the highest-risk levels (privileged change, physical action) are not implemented at all in this delivery. Real build: python -m build (see pyproject.toml).
notes: Read-only diagnostic CLI for the HYDRA-UMC/URTC ecosystem: ten OBSERVE-level tools with real handlers (storage, ports, processes, systemd units, logs, temperature, connectivity, manifests, pending updates, local knowledge search) behind a symbolic allow-list, secret redaction at every output boundary, JSON Schema contracts (ToolRequest, ToolResult, MaintenanceProposal, EvidenceBundle, PatchVerificationReport), a local TF-IDF knowledge index, evidence-bundle and proposal builders grounded only in valid tool results, and an adversarial test that a poisoned document can never produce a tool execution or leak a secret. Its test suite (`pytest tests`) passes in full. There is no inference engine, no transport for the escalation outbox and no HYDRA-UMC-SERVER integration yet - see the README ROADMAP.
